Some comments on birding in La Silla for future birds there: Birds can be pretty sparse and few appart around the domes and the astronomer lodges. There is a really good spot where I saw most passerines in this list that is about 300m below the dining + office building. The spot is at coordinates 29°15'08.5" south and 70°44'31.7" west. On google maps, you can see that the rocks have a different colour, and this where the water from the residence and offices is discarded. This leads to a constant trickle of water and an area that is 30x10m in size full of little water puddles. The birds concentrate there in pretty large number and one can get very good pictures of most species, especially when sitting and waiting for birds to come for water. This is the spot for the turca and earthcreeper. Observation Details: saw bird at dusk sitting one of the dust roads. took off in front of me and landed a few tens of meters away. I followed the bird a saw it taking off a few times. I saw very well the typical tail pattern.
Heard only, gave its typical call many times. Heard by a group of about 10 people.

This was a very memorable observation. At the time in 2000, visiting birders could rent rooms at the  Rancho Grande station. On one night I decided to sleep on the upper "deck", close to where the bird feeders were, in hope of hearing owls at night. The guacharo actually woke me in the middle of the night, with the very loud clicking sounds just over my head. While it matched the description of the guacharo sound in my field guide, and it was clearly coming from a bird flying around in the dark, I asked the biologists working at the station the following morning if that was indeed a guacharo as I had never observed that bird before. They confirmed the identification and told me that the bird was regularly coming around the Rancho Grande pretty much all nights.

Some comments on birding in La Silla for future birds there: Birds can be pretty sparse and few appart around the domes and the astronomer lodges. There is a really good spot where I saw most passerines in this list that is about 300m below the dining + office building. The spot is at coordinates 29°15'08.5" south and 70°44'31.7" west. On google maps, you can see that the rocks have a different colour, and this where the water from the residence and offices is discarded. This leads to a constant trickle of water and an area that is 30x10m in size full of little water puddles. The birds concentrate there in pretty large number and one can get very good pictures of most species, especially when sitting and waiting for birds to come for water. This is the spot for the turca and earthcreeper. Some comments on birding in La Silla for future birds there: Birds can be pretty sparse and few appart around the domes and the astronomer lodges. There is a really good spot where I saw most passerines in this list that is about 300m below the dining + office building. The spot is at coordinates 29°15'08.5" south and 70°44'31.7" west. On google maps, you can see that the rocks have a different colour, and this where the water from the residence and offices is discarded. This leads to a constant trickle of water and an area that is 30x10m in size full of little water puddles. The birds concentrate there in pretty large number and one can get very good pictures of most species, especially when sitting and waiting for birds to come for water. This is the spot for the turca and earthcreeper. J'avais initialement noté cette distance du fait que j'ai parcouru tous les chemins du jardin botanique, ainsi que la petite allée vers la "plage de l'ONU". En regardant les notes dans ebird sur la notation des distances, le 0.5km rapporté ici est plus réaliste parce que les sentiers parcourus à plusieurs reprises sont tout près les uns des autres. N'hésitez pas à mon contacter s'il y avait un autre souci avec cette liste.

Observation Details: D'abord j'ai pensé qu'il s'agissait d'un Pic mar à cause du front rouge, mais le sourcil noir point plutôt vers un Pic épeiche jeune, qui est beaucoup plus commun dans la région

Some comments on birding in La Silla for future birds there: Birds can be pretty sparse and few appart around the domes and the astronomer lodges. There is a really good spot where I saw most passerines in this list that is about 300m below the dining + office building. The spot is at coordinates 29°15'08.5" south and 70°44'31.7" west. On google maps, you can see that the rocks have a different colour, and this where the water from the residence and offices is discarded. This leads to a constant trickle of water and an area that is 30x10m in size full of little water puddles. The birds concentrate there in pretty large number and one can get very good pictures of most species, especially when sitting and waiting for birds to come for water. This is the spot for the turca and earthcreeper. Some comments on birding in La Silla for future birds there: Birds can be pretty sparse and few appart around the domes and the astronomer lodges. There is a really good spot where I saw most passerines in this list that is about 300m below the dining + office building. The spot is at coordinates 29°15'08.5" south and 70°44'31.7" west. On google maps, you can see that the rocks have a different colour, and this where the water from the residence and offices is discarded. This leads to a constant trickle of water and an area that is 30x10m in size full of little water puddles. The birds concentrate there in pretty large number and one can get very good pictures of most species, especially when sitting and waiting for birds to come for water. This is the spot for the turca and earthcreeper. Some comments on birding in La Silla for future birds there: Birds can be pretty sparse and few appart around the domes and the astronomer lodges. There is a really good spot where I saw most passerines in this list that is about 300m below the dining + office building. The spot is at coordinates 29°15'08.5" south and 70°44'31.7" west. On google maps, you can see that the rocks have a different colour, and this where the water from the residence and offices is discarded. This leads to a constant trickle of water and an area that is 30x10m in size full of little water puddles. The birds concentrate there in pretty large number and one can get very good pictures of most species, especially when sitting and waiting for birds to come for water. This is the spot for the turca and earthcreeper. Some comments on birding in La Silla for future birds there: Birds can be pretty sparse and few appart around the domes and the astronomer lodges. There is a really good spot where I saw most passerines in this list that is about 300m below the dining + office building. The spot is at coordinates 29°15'08.5" south and 70°44'31.7" west. On google maps, you can see that the rocks have a different colour, and this where the water from the residence and offices is discarded. This leads to a constant trickle of water and an area that is 30x10m in size full of little water puddles. The birds concentrate there in pretty large number and one can get very good pictures of most species, especially when sitting and waiting for birds to come for water. This is the spot for the turca and earthcreeper.
